title: Jethro
lead: Moses' father-in-law, the priest of Midian, who sheltered Moses, praised the LORD after the exodus and taught Moses to share the work of judging (Exodus 2–4; 18). Jewish tradition honors him as a model convert.

sections.b: He appears under several names: Reuel, who welcomes the runaway Moses and gives him his daughter Zipporah (Exodus 2:16–22); Jethro, whose flock Moses keeps (Exodus 3:1; 4:18) and who visits him in the wilderness (Exodus 18); and perhaps Hobab, whom Moses asks to be Israel's guide (Numbers 10:29–32; Judges 4:11). His descendants, the Kenites, settle with Judah (Judges 1:16), and Saul spares them when he attacks Amalek, because they had shown kindness to Israel (1 Samuel 15:6). Jeremiah 35 praises the Rechabites, a family linked to the Kenites (1 Chronicles 2:55), for their faithfulness.
